# Auto-Generated Dashboard Executive Summary

Generated by Amazon Quick's **Executive summary** feature (Create → Executive
summary) on the published **NovaTech Revenue Intelligence Dashboard**, with
*Allow executive summary* enabled at publish time. One summary per sheet,
reproduced verbatim below.

Each summary was then checked against `analysis/ground_truth.py`. Two of the
three are accurate; the third contains a clear error, documented at the end.

---

## Sheet 1 — Marketing Funnel

> The sheet provides a comprehensive overview of marketing campaign performance,
> tracking lead generation, spend efficiency, channel effectiveness, and funnel
> progression across multiple campaigns.
>
> - Despite a total campaign spend of $12.36M, only $1.13M in revenue was
>   attributed, suggesting significant room for ROI improvement.
> - Direct Mail achieved the highest Closed-Won Rate at 0.49, nearly doubling
>   Partner Referral at 0.31, yet Partner Referral drove the most leads at 807.
> - NovaPulse Launch led in attributed revenue at $394,156.59, while NovaEdge
>   Awareness severely underperformed, generating only $34,279.64 from
>   $1,518,785.09 in spend.
> - The funnel shows strong pipeline activity with 848 Qualified Leads and 412
>   Closed Won out of 2.24K total leads.

**Verification: ✅ accurate.** Every figure matches independently: spend
$12,359,497.34, attributed revenue $1,127,223.09, Direct Mail 49.0% vs Partner
Referral 31.1%, Partner Referral 807 leads, NovaPulse Launch $394,156.59,
NovaEdge Awareness $34,279.64 on $1,518,785.09, 848 Qualified Leads, 412 Closed
Won, 2,240 total.

## Sheet 2 — Sales Pipeline

> The sheet provides a comprehensive overview of sales deal performance, covering
> deal values, win rates, loss reasons, product breakdowns, monthly trends, and
> sales cycle duration.
>
> - The organization maintains a solid win rate of 0.63, with a total deal value
>   of 707.2K across all products, led by NovaPulse Professional at 208,724.
> - Monthly deal values peaked in Aug 2024 at 84,740 but have since declined,
>   with Jan 2025 dropping 27.5% from Dec 2024 and a 3-month compounded growth
>   rate of -3.02%.
> - The top loss reasons—Budget Constraints (31), Timing Not Right (33), and
>   Competitor Won (34)—are closely distributed, suggesting no single dominant
>   factor driving losses.
> - Deals take an average of 66.76 days to close, with an average deal value of
>   1.42K.

**Verification: ⚠️ mostly accurate, with one clear error — see below.**
Win rate 63.1%, total $707,201, NovaPulse Professional $208,724 and 66.8 average
days to close all match. The loss-reason bullet does not.

---

## Sheet 3 — Customer Health

> The sheet provides an overview of customer support performance, analyzing 3K
> total support tickets across metrics including resolution time, customer
> sentiment, product areas, and account-level activity.
>
> - Neutral sentiment dominates with 1,950 tickets, while negative tickets (684)
>   significantly outnumber positive ones (304), highlighting potential customer
>   experience concerns.
> - Average ticket resolution time is 58.69 hours, with remarkably similar
>   resolution times across low (59.41), high (58.11), and medium (57.99)
>   priority levels, suggesting priority has minimal impact on resolution speed.
> - Notifications leads ticket volume with 601 tickets, while Data Pipeline (310)
>   and Billing (329) have notably fewer.
> - The average negative sentiment rate of 0.23 indicates nearly a quarter of
>   interactions carry negative sentiment, warranting further investigation.

**Verification: ✅ accurate.** Negative 684 and positive 304 match exactly;
neutral is 1,953 against the stated 1,950 (a rounding presentation, not an
error). Resolution times 58.69 / 59.41 / 58.11 / 57.99, Notifications 601, Data
Pipeline 310, Billing 329 and the 22.8% negative rate all match.

Notably, the summary reached the **same conclusion I did** about priority
handling — "suggesting priority has minimal impact on resolution speed" —
without being prompted. That is the single most actionable finding on the sheet,
and the AI found it independently.

---

## The error in the Sales Pipeline summary

The summary states:

> "The top loss reasons—Budget Constraints (31), Timing Not Right (33), and
> Competitor Won (34)—are closely distributed, suggesting no single dominant
> factor driving losses."

Those are the **three smallest** loss reasons, not the top three. The actual
distribution across 184 lost deals is:

| Loss reason | Deals | Share of losses |
|---|---|---|
| **No Decision Made** | **43** | 23.4% |
| **Poor Product Fit** | **43** | 23.4% |
| Competitor Won | 34 | 18.5% |
| Timing Not Right | 33 | 17.9% |
| Budget Constraints | 31 | 16.8% |

The summary omitted the two largest categories entirely — and they are tied at
the top, together accounting for **46.7%** of all losses. Its conclusion that
there is "no single dominant factor" therefore points a reader away from the
real finding: nearly half of NovaTech's losses come from stalled decisions and
poor qualification, both of which are controllable earlier in the sales cycle.

This matters because it is the *opposite* of a rounding slip. The figures quoted
are individually correct, so nothing looks wrong; only checking the full ranking
reveals that the three cited are the bottom three. Quick Chat, asked the same
question directly, answered it correctly (see entry 5 of
`05_q_exploration_log.md`), which suggests the fault is in how the summary
selects what to highlight rather than in the underlying data.

**Conclusion for the team:** auto-generated summaries are a good first read and
they do surface real insights — the Customer Health summary found the
prioritisation problem unaided. But they are a starting point for review, not a
substitute for it, and superlatives like "top" deserve a check against the
ranking before being repeated to an executive.
